Build Quality-Control Settings

Source: R/qc_config.R
qc_config.Rd

Build the set of quality-control (QC) thresholds used by the whole pipeline. Every parameter has a default; override any of them through ....

qc_config(...)

Arguments

...

Parameters to override, as name = value. See Parameters.

Value

An object of class ppt_qc: a named list of parameters.

Parameters

Station transfer (pigs seen at several stations)

  • max_gap_days: maximum gap between two stations to treat the pig as transferred. A larger gap splits it into two animals. Default 3.

  • max_overlap_days: maximum time overlap between two stations. A larger overlap is treated as transponder misreads. Default 1.

  • max_jump_kg: body weight jump at the transfer that triggers a warning. Default 10.

Body weight records (used by clean_weight(), in this order)

  • weight_range: valid body weight of a single record, kg. Default c(15, 150).

  • adapt_days: adaptation period after entry, days (default 7). Body weights of the first adapt_days days after a pig's first visit are not used (qc_flag = "adaptation"). Their feed intake is kept: it counts for ADFI and FCR when these days lie inside stage_range (e.g. a pig that enters at 45 kg with a 30-120 kg stage), and not when the pig is still below the stage. 0 = off.

  • weight_track: track the weight of each pig back from the end of the test (default TRUE). The scale only counts a pig standing on it with all four feet, so a reading is too light only rarely, while several small pigs on the scale at once give readings that are too heavy. At the end of the test the pigs are large and only one fits on the scale, so the last days are the most reliable. Starting from the median of the last 3 recorded days and the daily gain of the last 14 days, the weight is tracked back day by day: a record is kept when it lies within track_tol (default 8%, at least 2 kg, widened by 0.5 kg per day without kept records) of the weight expected for that day; the daily gain is updated from the kept daily weights of the next 10 days. Other records are removed (qc_flag = "track"). Pigs with less than 7 recorded days or a test shorter than 14 days are not tracked.

  • weight_outlier: outlier methods applied to the remaining records, one or more of "rlm" (quadratic robust regression, bisquare weights; a record with a weight below rlm_cutoff is an outlier), "loess" (robust LOESS smooth; a record more than sd_max robust SDs from it is an outlier), "stl" (trend + weekly component of the daily median weight) and "sd" (quadratic least squares, sd_max SDs). Default c("rlm", "loess").

  • outlier_combine: "any" (outlier for any method, default) or "majority".

  • rlm_cutoff: default 0.5.

  • sd_max: default 3.

  • loess_span: smoothing span for LOESS and STL. Default 0.75.

Pig-level checks (used by clean_weight())

  • min_records, min_test_days, max_missing_rate: a pig with fewer valid weights (default 20), a shorter test (default 35 days) or a larger share of test days without a valid weight (default 0.30) is removed.

  • entry_weight_max, exit_weight_min: a pig entering heavier (default 65 kg) or leaving lighter (default 85 kg) is flagged as low confidence.

  • track_flag_share: a pig whose tracking removes more than this share of its records (default 0.4) is flagged as low confidence: the scale probably did not weigh it correctly for a long time (e.g. a faulty load cell).

  • smooth_r2_min: a pig whose valid weights fit their LOESS smooth with an R below this (default 0.99) is flagged as low confidence.

Growth, filled weights and ADG (used by calc_adg())

  • stage_range: body weight interval for ADG, ADFI and FCR, kg. Default c(30, 120).

  • curve_model: growth curve that fixes the stage start and end and fills the weights before the first and after the last recorded day: "poly2" (default), "poly1", "poly3" or "gompertz" (falls back to "poly2" when it does not converge). Missing days between recorded days are always filled by linear interpolation.

  • max_extrap_days: maximum extrapolation of the curve, days. Default 30.

Feeder errors (Casey et al. 2005, Table 3)

  • fiv_range: FIV-lo / FIV-hi, feed intake per visit, g.

  • fiv0_abs_max: FIV-0, maximum |FIV| for a 0 s visit, g.

  • duration_max: OTV-hi, maximum occupation time per visit, s.

  • speed_fiv_lo_max: FRV-hi-FIV-lo, maximum feeding rate for visits with 0 < FIV < 50 g, g/min.

  • speed_strict_max: FRV-hi-strict, maximum feeding rate when the preceding or following visit has FIV < -20 g, g/min.

  • speed_range: FRV-lo and FRV-hi, g/min.

  • idle_duration_max: FRV-0, maximum occupation time with no intake, s.

  • trough_diff_range: LWD / FWD, trough weight difference between subsequent visits, g.

  • max_unidentified_feed_kg: feed disappearance in unidentified visits per feeder above which a warning is given.

  • fiv_max_by_weight: optional table that replaces the upper limit of fiv_range (FIV-hi) by a limit that depends on body weight, and optionally on breed. Columns weight_from (kg, lower bound of the weight class), fiv_max (g) and optionally breed. See fiv_max_example(). NULL = off.

Daily feed intake (used by calc_adfi())

  • dfi_range: valid daily feed intake, kg.

  • dfi_quantile: optional, lower and upper quantile cut-offs (e.g. c(0.025, 0.99)). NULL = off.

  • dfi_correct: "lmm" (Jiao et al. 2014) or "none".

  • impute_method: how missing stage days are filled. "loess_lm" (default): gaps between recorded days of up to long_gap_days days are filled from a robust LOESS smooth of the daily intake, longer gaps and the days before the first / after the last recorded day by a linear regression of daily intake on body weight; "linear": linear interpolation between recorded days, the same regression at the ends.

  • long_gap_days: default 3.

Confidence flags (used by calc_fcr())

  • max_edge_extrap_days: a pig is "low_confidence" when its weights or its feed intake are filled over more than this many days at the start or the end of the stage. Default 15.

  • min_coverage: minimum share of stage days with recorded feed intake. Default 0.7.

  • bin_width: width of the body weight classes used for the segment checks of calc_fcr(), kg. Default 10.

  • min_bin_coverage_kg: an inner weight class whose recorded body weights span less than this many kg flags the pig. Default 6.

  • bin_fcr_limits: optional table of plausible FCR per weight class, columns weight_from (kg), fcr_min, fcr_max. See bin_fcr_example(). NULL = off.

References

Casey, D. S., Stern, H. S., & Dekkers, J. C. M. (2005). Identification of errors and factors associated with errors in data from electronic swine feeders. Journal of Animal Science, 83, 969-982.

Jiao, S., Maltecca, C., Gray, K. A., & Cassady, J. P. (2014). Feed intake, average daily gain, feed efficiency, and real-time ultrasound traits in Duroc pigs: I. Journal of Animal Science, 92, 2377-2386.
